Given my preference ordering of w > x > y > z, I would naturally want to propose to school w first. Additionally, I have the highest priority at school w (priority rank 1), which significantly increases my chances of being accepted there. Knowing that most applicants favor y > x > w > z, it is likely that many students will propose to school y first, potentially reducing competition for school w.

If I propose to school w and am accepted, I will be matched with my top choice. If I am rejected, I will move to my next preferred school, x. At school x, I have a priority rank of 2, which is still relatively high, giving me a good chance of being accepted if I need to propose there.

School y, while popular among other applicants, is my third preference. I have the highest priority there, but since I prefer schools w and x more, I will only propose to y if rejected by both w and x. Finally, school z is my least preferred option and will only be considered if all other proposals fail.

Therefore, my strategic approach is to follow my true preference order, given my priority rankings and the general preferences of other applicants.
